newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish central bank chief calls for tax freeze.
newsitem.headline: Polish central bank chief calls for tax freeze.

text.p: National Bank of Poland (NBP) President Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz said on Monday the country's budget would be best served if the government kept taxes unchanged next year.

"The best option for the budget was the government's (original) proposals to keep tax rates unchanged," Gronkiewicz-Waltz told a news conference at a private banking academy in the port city of Gdansk.

The government, which had agreed on a budget plan aiming at a deficit of 2.6 percent of GDP, last week proposed a modest tax cut which it said could keep the budget gap at 2.8 percent, unchanged from this year's planned level.
But in a surprise vote on Thursday the lower house of parliament passed a bill introducing a new lowest tax band of 17 percent for the lowest paid.
Gronkiewicz-Waltz said this bill would boost the deficit and inflation.
"With this four-level scale the budget deficit, according to NBP estimates, would be about three percent, which would translate into higher inflation of 15-16 percent next year," she said.
"This means that the budget would have to be rewritten to account for higher inflation," she added.

The central bank has said that already the 2.6 percent deficit would make reaching the government's 1997 inflation target of 13 percent difficult and the higher 2.8 percent shortfall made it very unlikely.
Government officials have signalled they hoped the Senate would overturn the parliament's decision and revert to the moderate government tax cut proposal.
